main_analogy: An open-book exam. In a closed-book exam a student must answer from memory and may guess; in an open-book exam the student first finds the right page in the textbook (retrieval), keeps that page next to the question (augmented), and then writes the answer from it (generation). The textbook = the knowledge source; finding the page = retrieval; the student = the LLM.

worked_example.scenario: Meena, a first-year student, asks her college's help chatbot about the merit scholarship. The chatbot uses RAG over the college notices.
documents: Chunk A: Applications for the merit scholarship close on 31 August.
Chunk B: To apply for the merit scholarship, you need at least 75% marks in Class 12.
Chunk C: The hostel fee must be paid by 15 July.
worked_example.question: What marks do I need for the merit scholarship, and what is the last date to apply?
worked_example.answer: You need at least 75% marks in Class 12. The last date to apply is 31 August.

quiz.q: Why can an LLM give a wrong answer about your college rules?
quiz.a: It never saw them during training, so it may guess.

quiz.q: What do the three words in RAG mean?
quiz.a: Retrieval = finding, Augmented = adding to the question, Generation = writing the answer.
A list of numbers that shows the meaning of a text.
No. It only adds information to the prompt.
